primary_source.author: J. E. Quibell
primary_source.title: Note on a Tomb Found at Tell er Roba
primary_source.journal: Annales du Service des Antiquites de l'Egypte

pre_inspector_provenance_fracture.observation: Local workmen had removed more than 350 faience ushabtis and probably other unknown objects before inspector Aly Effendi Habib intervened and recovered the ushabtis.
pre_inspector_provenance_fracture.implication: A missing or privately removed companion object remains historically possible, but no particular missing genital element is established.

burial_architecture.observation: The protected burial was beneath a limestone slab; the ushabtis and amulets were on top of the slab, while the gold was on the body below.

examples: gold foil sheet from the front of the body

phallus_sheath_function.observation: Quibell explicitly reports that gold foil was used to make rough sheaths covering the fingers, toes and phallus.
phallus_sheath_function.importance: This is direct primary excavation evidence that the phallus sheath belonged to the mummy's body-covering funerary gold technology rather than being identified in the excavation report as a detached Osirian reliquary.

additional_loss_signal.observation: Quibell judged that some small gold necklace figures were probably taken by the workmen.
additional_loss_signal.implication: The assemblage was not recovered with perfect completeness.

independent_modern_corroboration.observation: The Met states that beneath the slab was a mummy adorned with gold-leaf trappings and explicitly points to Cairo CG 53465-53469.

epistemic_update_for_CG53469.reason: The primary excavation report places the gold on the deceased's body and describes the phallus piece as one of a suite of rough gold-foil sheaths covering body parts. Therefore, if ancient organic tissue/resin is found within CG 53469, the first parsimonious interpretation must be tissue or embalming/funerary material associated with the deceased Nesbanebdjedet, unless independent evidence establishes a different identity/function.

why_CT_remains_high_value.question: What physically remains inside or attached to the detached gold sheath today?
why_CT_remains_high_value.identity_rule: A positive organic-density result establishes material content only; it does not establish identity as Osiris or any other named person/deity.

comparative_corpus_expansion.observation: A small gold phallus was reported between the legs of Padouneit's mummy, while other gold objects were distributed on the body.
comparative_corpus_expansion.caution: This is a small gold phallus/simulacrum, not demonstrated to be a hollow sheath like CG 53469.

comparative_corpus_expansion.observation: A mummy stored in the Egyptian Museum Cairo basement was moved to the museum garden and scanned non-destructively with a truck-mounted CT scanner. CT distinguished soft tissue, resin, linen packs, gilded materials and preserved male genitalia; the penis was seen within a linen sheath.
comparative_corpus_expansion.caution: This does not establish that CG 53469 has been scanned or that the museum will approve a scan.
